findings.claim: The JSDoc comment on isSafeMigrationCall still describes its use only for avoiding flagging the migration transaction as an unsupported-contract interaction, but the function is now also used to detect a version upgrade elsewhere, so the comment no longer reflects all of the function's callers and should describe what the function detects rather than who calls it.

The two new tests construct TransactionData using hand-written object literals instead of the already-imported txDataBuilder, which does not follow the preferred builder pattern for constructing test data even though it matches a neighboring test in the same file.

The zksync variant address newly matched by isSafeUpdateTxData (e.g. the 1.4.1 zksync address) is not covered by a test at this call site, relying only on tests of isSafeMigrationCall itself, so behavior specific to this caller is not pinned down by a test.

The updated check matches official migration addresses across every Safe version and variant and does not filter by chain ID, which is a deliberate widening of what is accepted even though it is constrained by requiring a trusted delegate-call target and a delegate call.
Removal of the wrapper div is a layout-only change with no accompanying test, and a screenshot demonstrating the visual fix should be included in the PR's visual summary.
